claims.text: Markus Franz published The Article Is Only the Beginning on 7 October 2026, proposing Liquid Utility and six Reader Skills, with a bridge closure as the example.
claims.quote: published by Markus Franz on 7 October 2026

claims.text: Liquid Utility is trusted journalistic knowledge combined with reusable methods and tools to help someone understand, follow or act on what matters to them.
claims.quote: trusted journalistic knowledge, combined with reusable methods and appropriate tools, to help someone understand, follow or act on what matters to them

claims.text: Franz delivers Liquid Utility through six Reader Skills: Understand, Update, Relate, Compare, Follow and Act.
claims.quote: Understand, Update, Relate, Compare, Follow and Act

claims.text: Franz replied that the story vault answers what we know and why it can be trusted, while Reader Skills answer what we can reliably help someone do with it.
claims.quote: Story Vault answers: what do we know, and why can it be trusted? Reader Skills answer: what can we reliably help someone do with it?

claims.text: The story vault keeps what was reported as a graph of claims tied to hashed evidence, sources with freshness, and versions where a correction supersedes a claim rather than deleting it.
claims.quote: versions, where a correction supersedes a claim rather than deleting it

claims.text: Over a pile of articles Update is a summarisation problem; over a story graph it is a diff, with new facts as new claim nodes and corrections as dated supersede edges.
claims.quote: Over a story graph, it is a diff.

claims.text: Follow is the same diff run on a schedule, and distinguishing could not check from nothing changed needs the freshness record the vault keeps.
claims.quote: That distinction needs freshness, a record of when each source was last checked against what the claim says

claims.text: Relate needs no personal profile: the reader's route is held on the reader's side and joined to the published graph there, so the newsroom does not learn which bus a family takes.
claims.quote: the newsroom serves claims and does not learn which bus a family takes

claims.text: Each safeguard Franz asks for is a property the graph has: a correction is a supersede edge every skill meets, and an anonymous source is flagged at the node so every projection redacts it.
claims.quote: an anonymous source is flagged at the node, and every projection, the article, a licensed extract, a skill's answer, redacts it without anybody having to remember

claims.text: In the bridge drawn as a graph, when the council moves the reopening date nothing is rewritten: one new claim supersedes the old end date and is at once the Update, the Follow alert and the correction.
claims.quote: nothing is rewritten: a new claim supersedes the old end date

claims.text: Franz's article adds locality, which the owner's monetisation had not mapped: the local paper is where trust and a brand form, because it is right about things readers can check themselves.
claims.quote: something into focus that I had thought about and not mapped

claims.text: People would pay small amounts, a pound a month or pence per check, for local reporting that is useful, and small from many people about the things nearest them is large in aggregate.
claims.quote: Small, from many people, about the things nearest to them, is a large amount in aggregate.

claims.text: Facts and their evidence travel up from a local contributor to an international wire, and every use pays back down the same edges, per use, in pence, automatically.
claims.quote: a national story that rests on a local claim can pay for it, per use, in pence, automatically

claims.text: The figure shows one illustrative split of one 10p use; the numbers are a proposal, the mechanism is not.
claims.quote: The figure shows one illustrative split of one 10p use.

claims.text: A page that cannot name its source cannot pay it.
claims.quote: a page that cannot name its source cannot pay it

claims.text: The verification API in the story vault design, a paid answer to did you report this and is it still current, is how a local newsroom gets paid for being right when a national desk asks.
claims.quote: it is how the local newsroom gets paid for being right

claims.text: Nothing on sgit.ai is wired to a payment rail today; the rails exist and the design names them, but no contributor has been paid through a graph yet.
claims.quote: Nothing on sgit.ai is wired to a payment rail today

claims.text: None of this works unless the service is better than the alternative for a real task, which is Franz's test and the right one.
claims.quote: none of this works unless the service is better than the alternative for a real task

claims.text: A publisher testing one maintained topic should keep it as a story vault from day one, record the contributors in the graph from day one, and publish the ledger of what was used and where the money went.
claims.quote: One local topic, one vault, one service, one ledger.

claims.text: The bridge, the readers, the journalism and the money are now a working simulation in a vault that since version 0.2 also counts the costs and two years of long tail.
claims.quote: which since version 0.2 also counts the costs, the two years of long tail, the stories after it and the trust they build

claims.text: The Mill Street Bridge vault has 23 views in four themes, the economics, an API and every assumption written down, fictional throughout.
claims.quote: 23 views in four themes, the economics, an API, and every assumption written down

claims.text: ChatGPT made an infographic of this article that is faithful on the argument but uses its own bridge dates and says credit the people who found it, where the article says pay them.
claims.quote: Its closing line says "credit the people who found it", where this article says pay them, and paying them is the point.

claims.text: The infographic of Franz's article drops his qualifiers that the six skills are a proposed framework and that reach, utility, relationship and reciprocity are a hypothesis to measure.
claims.quote: It drops his qualifiers, that the six skills are a proposed framework rather than a universal taxonomy

claims.text: Places, dates and hashes in the bridge figure are illustrative; the skills are Franz's, the mapping, the bridge graph and the payment chain are the newsroom's.
claims.quote: The mapping, the bridge graph, the payment chain and its illustrative split are ours.

claims.text: The article was drafted on 7 October 2026 by agent@riskmandate.ai, running Claude Opus 5.5, from Franz's article and reply and a voice note by Dinis Cruz, who holds editorial responsibility.
claims.quote: who is the author of the argument and the person with editorial responsibility
